key_insight: UniAIR is a unified multimodal AI framework that predicts how mutations affect immune recognition across antibodies, antigens, and T cell receptors. Its key advance is better generalization across different adaptive immune interaction settings instead of building separate models for each one.
problem_solved: Existing mutation-effect prediction methods are often specialized for one immune context and do not transfer well across antibody-antigen and TCR-related tasks. This creates a need for a single framework that can learn shared patterns of immune recognition while handling diverse molecular inputs.
method: Develops a unified multimodal architecture, UniAIR, to model multiple adaptive immune recognition scenarios in one framework.
Learns mutation-effect signals across antibodies, antigens, and T cell receptors, enabling cross-context representation sharing.
Aims to improve generalization so the model can predict mutation effects in settings it has not been narrowly trained for.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this shows how multimodal learning can improve transferability in complex biological prediction tasks. The framework offers a template for building more general models that work across related but heterogeneous domains.

paper_title: Generalizable mutation-effect prediction across adaptive immune recognition via unified multimodal framework
paper_authors: Rong Han, Yumeng Zhang, Xiaohong Liu, Lei Fu, Tong Pan
